proofs.proof_tex:
Write \(d_{a,u}(x)=m_{a,1,u}(x)-m_{a,0,u}(x)\).  If \(Q\) is a full-data extension, corrected no anticipation gives, for every clean \(c>t\) and every \(u\le t\),
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X]=m_{c,1,u}(X).
\]
No effect on ineligible units and consistency similarly give
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X]=m_{c,0,u}(X).
\]
The period-by-period parallel-gap restriction therefore implies \(d_{c,u}=d_{c',u}\) for every pair displayed in the statement.  Summing these equalities from \(g\) through \(t\) implies \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c'}\), proving necessity.

Conversely, suppose the displayed period-specific equalities hold.  Retained-cell overlap makes every conditional mean used below well defined.  On an enlargement carrying the observed \((Y,G,S,X)\), set all ineligible potential outcomes equal to one common ineligible path, taking that path equal to \(Y\) on units with \(S=0\).  For a retained eligible cohort \(a\), set \(Y_u(a,1)=Y_u\) on the event \(\{G=a,S=1\}\), and set its never-enabled path equal to the observed path before \(a\).  For a target cohort \(g\), recursively choose the post-\(g\) conditional means of its never-enabled eligible increments to be
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X]=m_{g,0,u}(X)+d_{c,u}(X),
\]
where \(c\) is any clean cohort occurring for the same \((g,u)\).  The assumed equalities make this choice independent of \(c\).  Unconstrained counterfactual coordinates may be set equal to these conditional means, with an independent centered bounded residual if an interior extension is desired.  This construction gives consistency, no ineligible effect, corrected mean no anticipation, and, equation by equation,
\[
E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid g,1,X]-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid g,0,X]=d_{c,u}(X)
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid c,1,X]-E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid c,0,X].
\]
Thus it is a full-data extension.

For a regular observed submodel with score \(s\), differentiation of \(d_{c,u}(x)-d_{c',u}(x)=0\) gives
\[
E_P[Z_{u;c,c'}(O)s(O)\mid X=x]=0.
\]
Because the preceding extension proves that these conditional-mean equations are the complete observed restrictions, the tangent space is the intersection of the kernels of these conditional linear maps.  In a Hilbert space, the orthocomplement of an intersection of closed kernels is the closed linear span of the adjoint ranges.  Those adjoint ranges are exactly the square-integrable measurable multiples of the displayed \(Z_{u;c,c'}\), proving the tangent characterization.

For two comparisons in the same target block, direct subtraction of the pairwise pseudo-outcomes gives
\[
R_{k,c}-R_{k,c'}=-\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}\sum_{u=g}^t Z_{u;c,c'}.
\]
Hence every generator of \(\mathcal C_P\) belongs to the period-specific normal closure, so \(\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp\).

Both failures of the original claim are explicit.  Take \(T=4\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{4,\infty\}\), degenerate \(X\), and positive probabilities for all retained cells.  Set \(d_{4,2}=1\), \(d_{4,3}=-1\), and \(d_{\infty,2}=d_{\infty,3}=0\), with all remaining conditional means bounded.  Then the two cumulative \(q\)'s agree because \(1+(-1)=0\), but the period-two equality fails; necessity above rules out a full-data extension.  At a different interior base law with all four gaps zero and conditionally independent, nondegenerate bounded residual increments in periods two and three, \(Z_{2;4,\infty}\) and \(Z_{3;4,\infty}\) are orthogonal and nonzero.  The full normal space contains their two-dimensional span, whereas \(\mathcal C_P\) contains only measurable multiples of their sum.  Thus the inclusion is strict.  This finite-support certificate disproves the asserted tangent exhaustion without changing the published period-by-period model.

Fix \(k=(g,t)\), \(c>t\), and \(u\in\{g,\ldots,t\}\).  Consistency gives
\[
m_{g,1,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\]
No effect on ineligible units and consistency give
\[
m_{g,0,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=g,S=0,X],\qquad
m_{c,0,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,0)\mid G=c,S=0,X].
\]
Because \(u<c\), corrected mean no anticipation at both \(u\) and \(u-1\), followed by consistency, gives
\[
m_{c,1,u}(X)=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=c,S=1,X].
\]
Subtracting the period-by-period parallel-gap equality from the first display yields
\[
m_{g,1,u}-m_{g,0,u}-m_{c,1,u}+m_{c,0,u}
=E_Q[\Delta Y_u(g,1)-\Delta Y_u(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\]
Summing over \(u=g,\ldots,t\) telescopes.  Mean no anticipation at \(g-1\) removes the lower endpoint, and hence
\[
q_{k,c}(X)=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1,X].
\]
Retained-cell overlap implies \(\pi_{g,1}>0\).  Multiplication by \(p_{g,1}(X)/\pi_{g,1}\), integration over \(P_X\), and iterated expectation give
\[
\theta_k(P)=\frac{E_P[p_{g,1}(X)q_{k,c}(X)]}{\pi_{g,1}}
=E_Q[Y_t(g,1)-Y_t(\infty,1)\mid G=g,S=1].
\]
The formula for \(\tau_\omega\) follows by its definition.  Finally, conditional residual means in the corrected pairwise score are zero, so
\[
E_P[\Psi_{k,c,P}(O)\mid X]=\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}\{q_{k,c}(X)-\theta_k(P)\};
\]
this is the centered ratio-functional OVS score and explicitly retains the derivative of \(\pi_{g,1}\).

Since \(A\) has full column rank and the columns of \(N\) are an orthonormal basis of \(\ker(A')\), every feasible vector has the unique representation \(b=b^0+Nz\).  Its conditional objective is
\[
(b^0+Nz)'\Gamma(b^0+Nz)=(b^0)'\Gamma b^0+2z'N'\Gamma b^0+z'Hz.
\]
Put \(g=N'\Gamma b^0\).  If \(v\in\ker H\), positive semidefiniteness gives
\[
0=v'Hv=(Nv)'\Gamma(Nv)=\|\Gamma^{1/2}Nv\|^2,
\]
so \(\Gamma Nv=0\) and \(v'g=(Nv)'\Gamma b^0=0\).  Thus \(g\perp\ker H\), which equals \(\operatorname{range}H\) for the symmetric finite-dimensional matrix \(H\).  The normal equation \(Hz=-g\) is therefore solvable, and its unique solution in \(\operatorname{range}H\) is \(z^\star=-H^\dagger g\).  This proves
\[
b^\star=b^0-NH^\dagger N'\Gamma b^0,
\quad A'b^\star=\omega,
\quad N'\Gamma b^\star=g-HH^\dagger g=0.
\]
Fixed rank and the separated positive spectrum make \(H^\dagger\) a measurable spectral function of \(H\), so the displayed selection is measurable.  Two minimizers differ by \(Nv\) with \(v\in\ker H\), equivalently by an element of \(\ker\Gamma\cap\ker A'\), proving the stated uniqueness.

If \(\Gamma\) is positive definite, the Lagrange equations are \(\Gamma b=A\lambda\) and \(A'b=\omega\).  Since \(A\) has full column rank, \(A'\Gamma^{-1}A\) is positive definite.  Solving gives
\[
b=\Gamma^{-1}A(A'\Gamma^{-1}A)^{-1}\omega,
\]
as claimed.

The corrected score and the observable equalities imply
\[
E_P[\Psi_P(O)\mid X]=Ah(X),\qquad
h_k(X)=\frac{p_{g,1}(X)}{\pi_{g,1}}\{q_{k,c_0(k)}(X)-\theta_k(P)\}.
\]
Hence every feasible loading has conditional mean
\[
E_P[b(X)'\Psi_P(O)\mid X]=b(X)'Ah(X)=\omega'h(X).
\]
The conditional variance formula and iterated variance now give
\[
\operatorname{Var}_P\{b(X)'\Psi_P(O)\}
=\operatorname{Var}_P\{\omega'h(X)\}+E_P[b(X)'\Gamma_P(X)b(X)].
\]
By the singular-operator lemma, \(b^\star\) minimizes the last integrand pointwise.  If \(d=b-b^\star\), then \(A'd=0\), so \(d=Nz\), and the pointwise projection equation gives
\[
d'\Gamma b^\star=z'N'\Gamma b^\star=0.
\]
Expanding \(b=b^\star+d\) proves the displayed Pythagorean identity and nonnegativity.  The corrected observable-equivalence result shows that the full normal closure can strictly contain \(\mathcal C_P\); projection only onto \(\mathcal C_P\) therefore cannot be called the full canonical projection in that generality.  This proves exactly the narrowed claim and refutes the omitted semiparametric lower-bound assertion.

There are finitely many covariate values, score coordinates, folds, and retained cells.  Cell overlap and the lower support-mass bound make every corresponding sample count of order \(n\) in probability.  The corrected score is a finite sum of outcome residuals multiplied by ratios bounded by overlap.  The conditional fourth-moment envelope and fixed \(T\) therefore imply a uniform conditional fourth moment for every score coordinate.  Each product \(\Psi_j\Psi_{j'}\) consequently has finite conditional variance.  Chebyshev's inequality applied to each of the finitely many cell means, followed by a union bound, gives an \(O_P(n^{-1/2})\) error for the oracle conditional first and second moments.

On the clipped overlap set, every propensity ratio is Lipschitz in its numerator and denominator, with a constant depending only on \(\varepsilon\).  Adding and subtracting the oracle propensities and regressions in each finite score coordinate and applying Hölder's inequality gives
\[
\|\widehat\Gamma-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}
\le O_P(n^{-1/2})+C\{r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}\}.
\]
All norms on the fixed finite support and in the fixed matrix dimension are equivalent, which proves the first assertion.  With parametric first stages, \(r_{\Gamma,n}=O(n^{-1/2})\).  For \(\tau_n=n^{-a}\),
\[
\frac{r_{\Gamma,n}}{\tau_n}=O(n^{-1/2+a})\to0,
\qquad r_{b,n}=O(n^{-1/2+a}).
\]
The loading perturbation argument gives rank recovery under fixed rank and the spectral gap.  Finally,
\[
r_{b,n}^2+r_{\Gamma,n}^2=O(n^{-1+2a}+n^{-1})=o(n^{-1/2})
\]
exactly when \(a<1/4\).  This proves the finite-support regime.  For a continuous covariate, estimating a conditional covariance in \(L_4(P_X)\) treats a product of two scores as the regression response; an outcome fourth moment supplies only a second moment for that response.  The original claimed \(L_4\) series rate therefore needs an additional tail or truncation analysis and is not established by the frozen premises.

Let \(E_\ell(x)=\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)-\Gamma(x)\|_{\mathrm{op}}\).  Weyl's inequality gives
\[
\max_j|\lambda_j\{N'\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}(x)N\}-\lambda_j\{H(x)\}|\le E_\ell(x).
\]
For all sufficiently large \(n\), \(\tau_n<\kappa/2\).  A rank error then implies \(E_\ell(x)>\tau_n\): a false positive above the zero spectral cluster requires an error exceeding \(\tau_n\), while a false negative from the positive cluster requires an error at least \(\kappa-\tau_n>\tau_n\).  Conditional Markov inequality and the covariance-rate assumption yield, uniformly over the fixed number of folds,
\[
P_X\{\widehat r^{-\ell}(X)\ne r_0\}
\le \tau_n^{-4}\|\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}-\Gamma\|_{P_X,4,\mathrm{op}}^4
=O_P\{(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)^4\}.
\]

Put \(g=N'\Gamma b^0=Hz^0\) with \(z^0=H^\dagger g\), whose existence was proved in the singular-operator lemma, and put \(\widehat g=N'\widehat\Gamma b^0\).  The spectral gap and the conditional fourth envelope bound \(\|z^0\|\) uniformly.  The retained inverse has norm at most \(\tau_n^{-1}\), and
\[
\widehat H_\tau^\dagger g
=\widehat H_\tau^\dagger H z^0
=\widehat P_\tau z^0+\widehat H_\tau^\dagger(H-\widehat H)z^0,
\]
where \(\widehat P_\tau=\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\widehat H\) is the retained spectral projector.  Together with \(\|\widehat g-g\|\le\|b^0\|E_\ell\), this identity gives the pointwise bound
\[
\|\widehat H_\tau^\dagger\widehat g-H^\dagger g\|
\le C\{1+E_\ell/\tau_n\}.
\]
On \(E_\ell\le\tau_n/2\), the rank is correct and standard resolvent identities on the separated positive cluster sharpen the right side to \(CE_\ell\).  On its complement, \(1\le2E_\ell/\tau_n\).  Combining the two cases therefore yields everywhere
\[
\|\widehat b^{-\ell}(x)-b^\star(x)\|
\le C E_\ell(x)/\tau_n.
\]
Taking \(L_4(P_X)\) and then \(L_2(P_X)\) norms proves the asserted \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n)\) rates.  Threshold separation makes them \(o_P(1)\).  On the correctly selected separated range, the inverse eigenvalues are bounded by \(2/\kappa\) and the resolvent identity directly gives the sharper \(O_P(r_{\Gamma,n})\) perturbation.

Write \(\eta=(p,m)\), and let \(R(\eta,\pi)\) denote the raw ratio pseudo-outcome.  Conditional on each training sample, cross-fitting makes the validation observations independent of \(\widehat\eta^{-\ell}\), \(\widehat\Gamma^{-\ell}\), and \(\widehat b^{-\ell}\).  Feasibility gives \(A'(\widehat b^{-\ell}-b^\star)=0\) exactly.  Because the oracle conditional mean of every raw score in target block \(k\) is the same, namely \(p_{g,1}(X)q_k(X)/\pi_{g,1}\),
\[
E_P[(\widehat b^{-\ell}(X)-b^\star(X))'R_P(O)\mid X,\text{training}]=0.
\]

For each cell term, add and subtract the true regression inside the estimated inverse-propensity residual.  The conditional expectation of the first-order propensity error and the first-order regression error vanishes, leaving a product.  Finite \(M,T\), overlap, and Hölder's inequality consequently give the foldwise bias bound
\[
\left|P\{b^{\star\prime}(R(\widehat\eta,\pi)-R(\eta,\pi))\}\right|\le C r_{p,n}r_{m,n},
\]
and, after inserting \(\widehat b-b^\star\), the conservative mixed bound
\[
\left|P\{(\widehat b-b^\star)'(R(\widehat\eta,\pi)-R(\eta,\pi))\}\right|
\le C r_{b,n}(r_{p,n}+r_{m,n}).
\]
Both are \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\) by the two product-rate assumptions.  The fourth-moment envelope, nuisance consistency, and the loading perturbation lemma also imply
\[
\|\widehat b'R(\widehat\eta,\pi)-b^{\star\prime}R(\eta,\pi)\|_{P,2}=o_P(1).
\]
Conditional Chebyshev inequality then makes the corresponding centered validation-fold empirical process \(o_P(n^{-1/2})\).

It remains to expand the empirical target-cell shares.  Since \(\pi_{g,1}\ge\varepsilon\),
\[
\widehat\pi_{g,1}^{-1}-\pi_{g,1}^{-1}
=-\pi_{g,1}^{-2}(\widehat\pi_{g,1}-\pi_{g,1})+O_P(n^{-1}).
\]
The mean numerator in every coordinate of target block \(k\) equals \(\pi_{g,1}\theta_k\), and feasibility sums its derivative with coefficient \(\omega_k\).  Thus the denominator expansion contributes
\[
-\sum_{k=(g,t)}\omega_k\frac{\theta_k}{\pi_{g,1}}\,n^{-1}\sum_{i=1}^n\{\mathbf 1_{g,1,i}-\pi_{g,1}\}.
\]
Combining this term with the raw-score empirical term gives exactly the corrected score \(b^\star(X)'\Psi_P(O)\).  Therefore
\[
\sqrt n(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}-\tau_\omega)
=n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n b^\star(X_i)'\Psi_P(O_i)+o_P(1).
\]
The corrected estimated influence values consistently include the displayed denominator term.  Their \(L_2(P)\) convergence and the conditional weak law give \(\widehat V_{\mathrm{eff}}\to_PV_\star\).  The cited i.i.d. central limit theorem, Slutsky's theorem, \(V_\star>0\), and the definition of the normal quantile yield the stated pointwise limit and coverage.  The canonical-gradient correction above establishes that this is score-family attainment, and identifies the additional tangent-exhaustion condition required for a semiparametric-efficiency interpretation.

Both \(b\) and \(b^\star(X)\) are feasible.  Their corrected scores therefore have the same conditional mean \(\omega'h(X)\).  The variance decomposition in the narrowed canonical-gradient result reduces their variance difference to the difference of conditional quadratic forms.  With \(d=b-b^\star=Nz\), the pointwise normal equation gives
\[
b'\Gamma b-b^{\star\prime}\Gamma b^\star
=2d'\Gamma b^\star+d'\Gamma d=d'\Gamma d=z'Hz.
\]
Integration proves the identity.  Also
\[
N'\Gamma b=N'\Gamma(b-b^\star)=Hz.
\]
If the residual is zero then \(z'Hz=0\), so the gap is zero.  Conversely, a zero expected gap and nonnegativity imply \(z'H(X)z=0\) almost surely.  Positive semidefiniteness then gives \(H(X)z=0\), hence the residual is zero almost surely.  Applying this argument to the Moore--Penrose definitions of \(b^{\mathrm{OVS}}\) and \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\) proves both comparator characterizations.  The final qualification follows from the strict tangent-space inclusion already proved.

Use the bounded interior law from the tangent counterexample with \(T=4\), \(\mathcal K=\{(2,3)\}\), \(\mathcal J_{(2,3)}=\{4,\infty\}\), degenerate \(X\), zero conditional gaps, and independent nondegenerate period-two and period-three residual contrasts \(Z_2=Z_{2;4,\infty}\) and \(Z_3=Z_{3;4,\infty}\), scaled to have the same variance.  The corrected observable-equivalence result gives
\[
Z_2,Z_3\in\mathcal T_P^\perp,
\qquad E_P[Z_2Z_3]=0,
\qquad E_P[Z_2^2]=E_P[Z_3^2]>0.
\]
On the other hand, the frozen aggregate normal is proportional to \(Z_2+Z_3\).  Choose the bounded dictionary coordinate \(v_1=Z_2-Z_3\).  Its covariance with the aggregate normal is zero, so the coefficient \(a_{1,P}\) in the frozen definition is zero and
\[
t_{1,P}=v_1-E_P[v_1]=Z_2-Z_3.
\]
This function is nonzero and belongs to \(\mathcal T_P^\perp\).  At an interior restricted law, \(\mathcal T_P\cap\mathcal T_P^\perp=\{0\}\), hence \(t_{1,P}\notin\mathcal T_P\).  This directly contradicts the load-bearing assertion in the frozen sieve definition.  Independently, the score correction proves that the covariance derivative must be formed from \(\Psi\), not from the raw ratio pseudo-outcome \(R\).  Therefore the proposed sieve representer is not the Riesz representer used in the claimed expansion, and no sequence of the stated Gram or approximation assumptions repairs the fact that its coordinates are outside the tangent space.  The counterexample is bounded, has positive cell probabilities, and can be given arbitrarily small independent outcome noise, so it is not a boundary artifact.  The three repairs stated in the narrowed theorem are therefore necessary before a pointwise central limit theorem can be proved.

The construction has \(p_{a,s}(x)=1/6\) for every \(a\in\{2,3,\infty\}\), \(s\in\{0,1\}\), and \(x\in\{-1,1\}\), so overlap holds and \(\pi_{2,1}=1/6\).  The outcomes are bounded because \(|Z_t^{\mathrm w}|\le1/8\) and \(|\delta|<1/8\).  Consistency holds by construction.  When \(s=0\), the treatment term vanishes for every adoption date, proving no ineligible effect.  Before adoption the treatment term also vanishes, proving no anticipation pathwise for every retained cohort.  Finally, the law of \((U^{\mathrm w},V^{\mathrm w})\) depends on \((G,X)\) but not on \(S\).  Thus the never-enabled eligibility gap is zero in every cohort and period, which proves every conditional parallel-gap restriction.  Hence \(Q^{\mathrm{bin}}_{r,\delta}\in\mathcal M\).

The conditional means are
\[
m_{2,s,2}=s\delta,\quad m_{3,s,3}=s\delta,
\]
with every other retained one-step treatment term equal to zero.  Since \(E[U^{\mathrm w}\mid G,X]=E[V^{\mathrm w}\mid G,X]=0\), all three conditional DDD contrasts and both targets equal \(\delta\).  The corrected score therefore contains no residual categorical term proportional to \(\delta\).  Put \(a=3/4\).  In the declared score order, the nonzero residual values are
\[
\begin{array}{c|ccc}
(G,S)&\Psi_{(2,2),3}&\Psi_{(2,2),\infty}&\Psi_{(2,3),\infty}\\ \hline
(2,1)&aU^{\mathrm w}&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(2,0)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(3,1)&-aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(3,0)&aU^{\mathrm w}&0&0\\
(\infty,1)&0&-aU^{\mathrm w}&-aV^{\mathrm w}\\
(\infty,0)&0&aU^{\mathrm w}&aV^{\mathrm w}.
\end{array}
\]
Every row has conditional probability \(1/6\).  Also
\[
E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=2]=E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=3]=0,
\quad E[U^{\mathrm w}V^{\mathrm w}\mid X=x,G=\infty]=xr.
\]
Multiplying the entries row by row gives
\[
\Gamma(x)=\frac{3}{16}\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}.
\]

Feasibility is \(b_1+b_2=\omega_1\), \(b_3=\omega_2\), so write
\[
b(q)=(\omega_1/2+q,\ \omega_1/2-q,\ \omega_2)'.
\]
Differentiating its conditional quadratic form gives
\[
\frac{d}{dq}\{b(q)'\Gamma(x)b(q)\}=\frac{3}{16}\{4q-2xr\omega_2\}.
\]
The second derivative is \(3/4>0\), hence the unique optimum is \(q^\star(x)=xr\omega_2/2\), which yields the displayed \(b^\star(x)\).  The eigenvalues follow from
\[
\det\left\{\begin{pmatrix}2&1&0\\1&2&xr\\0&xr&2\end{pmatrix}-\lambda I\right\}
=(2-\lambda)\{(2-\lambda)^2-(1+r^2)\};
\]
they are \(2\) and \(2\pm\sqrt{1+r^2}\), multiplied by \(3/16\).  Since \(r^2<7/9\),
\[
\frac{3}{16}\{2-\sqrt{1+r^2}\}>\frac18.
\]

Because \(E[X]=0\), the unconditional covariance has its \((2,3)\) entry equal to zero.  The joint constant objective and the first OVS block are therefore uniquely minimized at \(q=0\), while the third coordinate is fixed; both named constant loadings equal \((\omega_1/2,\omega_1/2,\omega_2)'\).  Their displacement from the conditional optimum is \((-xr\omega_2/2,xr\omega_2/2,0)'\).  Direct quadratic evaluation gives
\[
\Delta=E_P\left[\frac{3}{16}\,2\left(\frac{r\omega_2}{2}\right)^2\right]
=\frac{3r^2\omega_2^2}{32}>0.
\]
At \(r=\omega_2=1/2\), this is \(3/512\).  More generally, strict convexity shows that every constant \(q\ne0\) has still larger average loss, so the best constant itself already loses strictly.  In this particular architecture the only overidentifying restriction is the single period-two comparison between cohorts \(3\) and \(\infty\); its residual contrast is exactly \(N'R\).  Thus the period-specific and aggregate tangent-normal closures coincide here, so the general tangent-exhaustion defect does not invalidate this binary early-kill calculation.

When every block is a singleton, the incidence matrix is the identity after the fixed target ordering.  Hence \(M=K_0\), \(\ker(A')=\{0\}\), and the zero-column convention gives no columns in \(N\).  The equation \(A'b=\omega\) has exactly one solution, so the conditional and constant loading problems coincide.

If \(X\) is degenerate, \(\Gamma(X)=\Gamma\) and \(h(X)\) is constant.  The law-of-total-covariance identity gives
\[
\Omega=\Gamma+A E_P[h(X)h(X)']A'.
\]
For every feasible \(b\), the second quadratic term is
\[
b'AE_P[hh']A'b=\omega'E_P[hh']\omega,
\]
which is independent of \(b\).  Therefore the minimizers of \(b'\Omega b\) and \(b'\Gamma b\) over \(A'b=\omega\) coincide.  Because \(b^0\) is orthogonal to \(\operatorname{col}N\), the quotient selection \(N'(b-b^0)\in\operatorname{range}H\) is the minimum-Euclidean-norm member of that solution set.  It agrees with the Moore--Penrose convention defining \(b^{\mathrm{const}}\).

added_lemmas.statement: If \(Z_1,Z_2,\ldots\) are independent and identically distributed real random variables with \(E[Z_1]=0\) and \(0<E[Z_1^2]<\infty\), then \(n^{-1/2}\sum_{i=1}^n Z_i\Rightarrow N(0,E[Z_1^2])\).

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Suppose that mean no anticipation applies to every finite cohort used either as a target cohort or as a clean comparison cohort.  An observed law \(P\) admits a full-data extension in the target-indexed period-by-period DDD model if and only if, for every two indices \(k=(g,t)\) and \(k'=(g,t')\), every \(u\in\{g,\ldots,\min(t,t')\}\), and every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\) and \(c'\in\mathcal J_{k'}\),
\[
m_{c,1,u}(X)-m_{c,0,u}(X)=m_{c',1,u}(X)-m_{c',0,u}(X)\qquad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
At an interior law the tangent orthocomplement is the closed span of measurable multiples of the period-specific residual contrasts
\[
Z_{u;c,c'}(O)=\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,1}}{p_{c,1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,1,u}(X)\}-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,0}}{p_{c,0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,0,u}(X)\}-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',1}}{p_{c',1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',1,u}(X)\}+\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',0}}{p_{c',0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',0,u}(X)\}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp\), but equality need not hold.  The cumulative equalities \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c_0(k)}\) are necessary but, when a target spans more than one period, are not sufficient for a full-data extension and do not exhaust the tangent restrictions.
proposed_statement_changes.reason: The period-by-period maintained restrictions imply one observable equality for every period.  Equality only of their cumulative sums \(q_{k,c}\) is insufficient, and the aggregate closure generated by \(N'R\) can omit linearly independent period-specific normal directions.  The proof supplies bounded finite-support witnesses for both failures.

proposed_statement_changes.proposed:
Let \(P\) satisfy the observable clean-comparison equalities and admit \(Q\in\mathcal M\) that induces \(P\), with mean no anticipation imposed on every retained finite target or comparison cohort.  For every \(k=(g,t)\in\mathcal K\) and every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\),
\[

proposed.statement:
Suppose that mean no anticipation applies to every finite cohort used either as a target cohort or as a clean comparison cohort.  An observed law \(P\) admits a full-data extension in the target-indexed period-by-period DDD model if and only if, for every two indices \(k=(g,t)\) and \(k'=(g,t')\), every \(u\in\{g,\ldots,\min(t,t')\}\), and every \(c\in\mathcal J_k\) and \(c'\in\mathcal J_{k'}\),
\[
m_{c,1,u}(X)-m_{c,0,u}(X)=m_{c',1,u}(X)-m_{c',0,u}(X)\qquad P_X\text{-almost surely}.
\]
At an interior law the tangent orthocomplement is the closed span of measurable multiples of the period-specific residual contrasts
\[
Z_{u;c,c'}(O)=\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,1}}{p_{c,1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,1,u}(X)\}-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c,0}}{p_{c,0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c,0,u}(X)\}-\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',1}}{p_{c',1}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',1,u}(X)\}+\frac{\mathbf 1_{c',0}}{p_{c',0}(X)}\{\Delta Y_u-m_{c',0,u}(X)\}.
\]
Consequently \(\mathcal C_P\subseteq\mathcal T_P^\perp\), but equality need not hold.  The cumulative equalities \(q_{k,c}=q_{k,c_0(k)}\) are necessary but, when a target spans more than one period, are not sufficient for a full-data extension and do not exhaust the tangent restrictions.

open_obligations.what_is_open: A nontrivial uniformly valid, rank-adaptive confidence interval has not been characterized because the question does not specify a uniform law class, a length or power requirement, or local eigenvalue and nuisance-rate envelopes.
open_obligations.obstruction: At rank-changing laws the Moore--Penrose loading is discontinuous, while coverage alone admits the vacuous interval \(\mathbb R\).  Without a non-vacuity criterion and a local sequence class, the intended adaptation problem is not a well-posed mathematical yes-or-no statement.
open_obligations.attempted: The fixed-rank perturbation proof was extended to eigenvalues approaching zero.  Its bound necessarily contains the reciprocal selected eigenvalue, so neither the learned-loading remainder nor a stable Gaussian critical value is uniform.  A negative adaptation theorem would require a specified local experiment and an interval-length criterion; a positive theorem would require explicit eigenvalue-decay and learner-rate restrictions.
open_obligations.partial_result: On every fixed-rank law with positive spectrum separated by \(\kappa>0\), the existing threshold rule with \(r_{\Gamma,n}/\tau_n\to0\) recovers rank and gives the pointwise expansion proved for \(\widehat\tau_{\mathrm{eff}}\).  No uniform claim is made as \(\kappa\downarrow0\).
